English language requirements for UK universities usually range from IELTS 6.0 to 7.0. More selective or language-intensive courses may ask for IELTS 7.5, while some foundation and pathway programmes accept lower scores.

IELTS is not the only route. Depending on the university and course, you may also use TOEFL iBT, PTE Academic, Cambridge English, LanguageCert, Duolingo, Oxford ELLT or an eligible school qualification. Some institutions accept a previous English-medium degree or a Medium of Instruction letter.

This guide explains the current rules, typical scores, accepted tests, country-specific waivers, costs and the major TOEFL change introduced in 2026. It is a practical starting point for students preparing to study at a British university.

Quick answer: Most bachelor's courses ask for IELTS 6.0 to 6.5. Many master's courses require 6.5 to 7.0. Medicine, dentistry, law, education and some humanities programmes may ask for 7.0 to 7.5, often with strict minimum scores in all four skills.

How We Checked This Guide

We reviewed current UK government guidance, official university admissions pages and information published by English test providers.

The university examples were checked in July 2026. Requirements can still change by course, intake and applicant profile, so use the exact course page and your offer letter as the final authority.

These are planning benchmarks, not national minimum scores.

A university can operate several English bands at the same time. UCL, for example, uses five proficiency levels. Manchester publishes typical overall bands from 5.5 to 7.5 or above, but each course sets its own requirement.

One detail catches students surprisingly often: a strong overall score cannot always compensate for a weak component.

You could hold IELTS 7.0 overall and still miss an offer requiring 6.5 in every skill because your Writing score is 6.0. Check both the overall score and every component before you book another test.

IELTS recommends a two-year validity period, although an organisation may choose to accept an older result. Universities can also set their own reference date, such as requiring the test to remain valid when the course begins.

A Practical Example

Suppose a university accepts the Duolingo English Test for direct entry to a master's course.

Which English Test Should You Choose?

IELTS Academic for the widest acceptance

PTE for fast, computer-based testing

PTE Academic assesses all four skills on a computer. Pearson says most candidates receive results within two business days, although some cases take up to five. PTE Academic UKVI is the approved SELT version for relevant routes. Check which UK institutions currently recognise PTE before booking.

TOEFL when the format suits you

TOEFL introduced a 1 to 6 scale on 21 January 2026. During a two-year transition, score reports also provide a comparable overall score on the older 0 to 120 scale.

Universities have responded differently. UCL accepts the revised test. Oxford currently does not accept tests taken from 21 January 2026 while it reviews the change. Cambridge says the revised test is not suitable for undergraduate entry. Manchester does not accept the TOEFL Home Edition. Check the test date as carefully as the score.

Duolingo only after course-level confirmation

Duolingo offers a convenient online format, but it is not a UKVI-approved SELT and acceptance may vary between departments. Use the current overview of institutions considering Duolingo as a shortlist, then verify your course.

The range is wide for a reason. A computer science course and a clinical programme at the same institution may assess language risk very differently.

Do not copy a university-wide score into your application plan until you have opened the exact course page.

Can You Study in the UK Without IELTS?

Yes, in some cases. “Without IELTS” does not mean without evidence of English.

A university might accept:

  • PTE, TOEFL or another recognised test
  • an eligible secondary-school English qualification
  • a degree taught and assessed in English
  • a Medium of Instruction certificate
  • a university interview or internal assessment
  • successful completion of a pre-sessional programme

Students comparing these routes can review the practical alternatives to IELTS.

Can an MOI Certificate Replace an English Test?

It can, but only when the university's policy allows it.

Consider two Bangladeshi applicants with similar academic histories. One university may accept an MOI document from selected institutions, while another may reject MOI as evidence and require an approved external test.

Same country. Similar document. Different decision.

A generic MOI certificate cannot guarantee a waiver. Read how universities assess previous English-medium education, then secure written confirmation for your course.

What the Country Rules Mean in Practice

For Bangladesh, there is no universal HSC percentage or MOI rule. One university may consider HSC English or MOI from selected institutions, while another asks for an external test.

For India, some universities accept Standard XII English, but the board, score and course matter. Manchester may consider Standard XII English depending on the board and result, but does not accept a university MOI letter by itself.

For Nigeria, selected universities accept WAEC, WASSCE or NECO English. Lancaster, for example, lists C6 or above for relevant postgraduate applicants and explains how results should be verified. Other universities may set a different grade or validity rule.

These differences make written course-level confirmation essential.

English Test and Pre-Sessional Course Costs

There is no single worldwide IELTS, TOEFL, PTE or LanguageCert fee. Your country, test type, taxes, booking date and test centre determine the amount.

As a current reference point, LanguageCert lists its Academic SELT from US$270. Local fees for IELTS, TOEFL and PTE should always be checked through the provider's official booking system.

A pre-sessional course usually costs much more than one test retake. It can still be the better choice when a student needs academic writing, seminar participation and research skills rather than another attempt at the same exam.

The cheapest test is not always the cheapest route. A low-cost online exam becomes an expensive mistake when your chosen course rejects it.

What If Your English Score Is Too Low?

Start with the wording in your offer.

Check the required overall score, the minimum for each skill, accepted test formats, test validity and whether the university accepts IELTS One Skill Retake.

Then choose the smallest sensible intervention. You may retake the complete exam, retake one skill where accepted, switch to another recognised test, join a pre-sessional programme or submit an eligible qualification that the university has not yet assessed.

IELTS One Skill Retake lets a candidate retake one of the four skills. University acceptance still varies, so confirm the policy before booking.

In real admissions work, students often say, “I need 6.5,” as though the other four numbers do not exist. Admissions teams read the full score report.

You should too.

Common Mistakes That Delay Admission

Avoid these common errors:

  • booking standard IELTS when a below-degree route requires a SELT
  • checking the overall score but ignoring component minimums
  • using a result that expires before the course begins
  • assuming every university accepts online tests
  • treating MOI as an automatic waiver
  • reading a general university page but not the exact course page

A course asking for 6.5 overall with 6.0 in each skill will not normally accept 7.0 overall with 5.5 in Writing. Small details decide the outcome, so check them before submitting evidence.

How to Check Your Exact English Requirement

1. Open the exact course page

Do not stop at a Google snippet or a third-party table. Find the page for the exact degree, year and intake.

2. Record the full requirement

Write down the overall score and all four component scores. Note whether the course uses a standard, higher, band or profile system.

3. Check the test version

Confirm whether the university accepts standard or UKVI IELTS, IELTS Online, TOEFL Home Edition, the revised TOEFL, PTE Academic Online, One Skill Retake, online LanguageCert or ELLT.

4. Check validity

Your result may need to remain valid when the course begins, not only when you apply.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the English language requirements for UK universities in 2026?

Most undergraduate degrees require IELTS 6.0 to 6.5 or an accepted equivalent. Many postgraduate courses ask for 6.5 to 7.0. Selective and language-intensive programmes may require 7.0 to 7.5. The exact course page sets the final score.

Is IELTS compulsory for UK universities?

No. Universities may accept TOEFL, PTE, Cambridge English, LanguageCert, Duolingo, Oxford ELLT, school qualifications or previous English-medium study. Acceptance varies by institution and course.

Can a university require more English than UKVI?

Do UK universities accept TOEFL Home Edition?

Some do and others do not. UCL accepts it under published conditions. Manchester does not. Oxford's policy also depends on whether the test was taken before or from 21 January 2026.

What changed with TOEFL in 2026?

TOEFL introduced a 1 to 6 score scale on 21 January 2026. During the transition, reports also include a comparable overall result on the older 0 to 120 scale.

Can I combine results from two IELTS tests?

Usually not unless the university explicitly accepts score combining or an eligible One Skill Retake. Many institutions require the overall and component scores in one accepted result.

How long are IELTS, TOEFL and PTE results valid?

Universities commonly use a two-year validity period, although the reference date varies. Check whether the result must remain valid when the course starts.

Can Bangladeshi students use HSC English or MOI?

Selected universities may consider HSC English, MOI or a previous English-medium degree. Others require an external test. No universal HSC score or MOI policy covers every UK university.

Is a pre-sessional course guaranteed to lead to my degree?

No universal guarantee applies. You must meet the course's attendance, assessment and progression conditions. Read the terms before paying a deposit.

Final Check Before You Book a Test

Meeting the English language requirements for UK universities does not start with choosing the most popular exam.

Start with your exact course.

Bring your course name, intended intake and latest English result. A specific case produces a useful answer and a much clearer next step.
